audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer rows disagreed with content win[]: five read "Skill" and the last two read "Ryze", against win[] which is Akali on every row.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Akali x7 and the matchup wins 52.41% over 1868 games. Rows 6 and 7 in particular rendered the opposite winner to the content layer.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].side = Akali as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early described his kit as "Q spellbind, W snare, E dash-blink", and spikes[1] referred to "Desperate Power stacks".
audit.why: Overload is a line projectile, Rune Prison is a targeted cage, and Spell Flux is a targeted debuff orb — Ryze has no dash and no blink anywhere in his kit. Desperate Power is not an ability he has; his ultimate is Realm Warp.
audit.corrected: Kit described correctly; the level 6 spike keyed to Spell Flux instead of a nonexistent stacking buff.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction was absent: Rune Prison only ROOTS if the target already has Flux on them — otherwise it merely damages and slows.
audit.why: The whole page treated the root as unconditional and told the player to fear it whenever it is up. The real gate is Spell Flux (615 range, 2.5-3.5s), and dodging the orb downgrades the cage to a slow. Second unstated interaction: both Rune Prison and Spell Flux are target-locked, and Twilight Shroud makes Akali unable to be selected — so inside the smoke the only spell that can reach her is the Overload line.
audit.corrected: Dodge Spell Flux and the root never happens; shroud denies W and E outright.
sources: enemyKit W text ("If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted")

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Rune Prison a "fifteen-second" cooldown.
audit.why: It is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. Overload is 5s and resets off his other casts; Spell Flux is 2.5-3.5s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d.

edits.before: He pokes until you shroud, then the lane belongs to the smoke — trade in obscured windows and energy-walk the rest.
edits.after: His W and E both need a target, so the shroud blanks them — only the Overload line finds you inside the smoke.

edits.before: Survive the poke, then win every shrouded exchange until one becomes a kill. Keep one eye on Rune Prison (Root) and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Survive the poke, then win every shrouded exchange until one becomes a kill. Dodge Spell Flux and Rune Prison never roots — that is the whole lane.

edits.before: Ryze wins by landing Rune Prison (Root), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Ryze wins by sticking Spell Flux on you, rooting with Rune Prison, and chaining Overload while you cannot move.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Check it before every step-up. - W Twilight Shroud is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Rune Prison: 9-11s, 615 range, and it only roots if Spell Flux is already on you — dodge the orb and the cage is just a slow. - Spell Flux: 2.5-3.5s, but it is target-locked, so inside the shroud he cannot apply it at all.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Carry by taking him alone — Ryze has no dash, so a shrouded flank puts you on him before the root lands.

edits.before: If Ryze gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Rune Prison (Root) extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q range and stay relevant through shroud picks.
edits.after: If Ryze gets a kill, stay outside 615 units — that is the reach of both Spell Flux and Rune Prison. Two kills: farm at Q range, and go only when he is alone with his orb spent on the wave.

edits.before: Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Rune Prison only roots if Spell Flux is on you — dodge the orb and it is just a slow.

edits.before: Ryze burns Rune Prison (Root) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Ryze burns Rune Prison on nothing — that is your ten-second invitation.

edits.before: Track Ryze’s Rune Prison (Root): Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Spell Flux, not the cage: Rune Prison roots only a Fluxed target, and both are target-locked, so the shroud denies them.

edits.before: His Realm Warp is a map-pressure tool, not a lane spike, so 6 changes little in-lane — you still hold the burst advantage if he overextends to land Desperate Power stacks.
edits.after: His Realm Warp is a map-pressure tool, not a lane spike, so 6 changes little in-lane — you still hold the burst advantage whenever he steps up to land Spell Flux.

edits.before: Ryze's early combo (Q spellbind, W snare, E dash-blink) is mana-starved and telegraphed — every root miss is a full punish window for your Q-W-E-R combo. You out-trade him in every short exchange from level 3 onward since he simply cannot burst you before your Shroud stealth closes the gap. Farm patiently, dodge his root, and go all-in the instant he whiffs Rune Prison.
edits.after: Ryze's early combo (Spell Flux orb, then a rooting Rune Prison, then Overload) is mana-starved and telegraphed — every missed orb is a full punish window for your Q-W-E-R combo. You out-trade him in every short exchange from level 3 onward since he simply cannot burst you before your Shroud stealth closes the gap. Farm patiently, dodge his orb, and all-in the instant he whiffs Rune Prison.

edits.before: You beat his early all-in outright since his root is mana-costly and easy to punish on a whiff with your full combo
edits.after: You beat his early all-in outright: Rune Prison only roots through Spell Flux, and both cost heavy mana at level 1

edits.before: Land root off Overload-Rune Prison chains to peel you off before you close the gap
edits.after: Land Spell Flux first so that Rune Prison roots you instead of merely slowing

notes: The page's central claim — that Rune Prison is a root you must always respect — is conditional in Riot's own text: it roots ONLY a target already carrying Flux, and otherwise just slows. Dodging Spell Flux is therefore the actual skill of the lane, and the page never mentioned it. Also removed "Desperate Power" (not an ability Ryze has) and the invented "E dash-blink" (he has no dash at all). Templated fields left in place: breakdown.wave, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, ahead, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.late. Unverified: whether Realm Warp's portal can be used to escape after Akali commits, and whether Overload's Flux-bonus damage still applies to a target inside Twilight Shroud.
